form.label: Coverage
form.description: What the feed can and cannot say anything about. Read this before trusting a low finding count.

div.b: A low finding count is not the same as a secure fleet.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_hostecostate_lookup | where hostname="__fleet__" | table type, components | sort 50000 - components | head 40

viz.option: No inventory received. Nothing can be assessed until swinv data reaches the index.

div.span: Click an ecosystem above to narrow everything below it.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_hostecostate_lookup | where hostname="__fleet__" | search $eco_filter$ | rename instances AS components | stats sum(components) AS components, sum(with_identifier) AS with_identifier BY type | eval without_identifier = components - with_identifier | eval identifier_pct = round(with_identifier * 100 / components, 1) | sort 50000 - components | rename type AS "Ecosystem", components AS "Components", with_identifier AS "With purl/cpe", without_identifier AS "No identifier", identifier_pct AS "Identifiable %"

| `riskability_open_findings` | search ecosystem=$eco_name|s$ | eval root = if(scope_id!="", scope_id, "host") | stats dc(package) AS packages, dc(cve_id) AS cves BY root, hostname | sort 50000 - packages | rename root AS "Root", hostname AS "Host", packages AS "Packages", cves AS "CVEs"

| inputlookup riskability_hostecostate_lookup | where hostname="__fleet__" | search $eco_filter$ | stats sum(instances) AS components, sum(cpe_ident) AS cpe_ident BY type | append [| `riskability_feed_ecosystems` | rename ecosystem AS type] | eventstats max(eval(if(type=="cpe", feed_ranges, null()))) AS cpe_ranges | stats max(components) AS components, max(cpe_ident) AS cpe_ident, max(feed_packages) AS feed_packages, max(feed_ranges) AS feed_ranges, max(cpe_ranges) AS cpe_ranges BY type | where isnotnull(components) | eval feed_packages = coalesce(feed_packages, 0), feed_ranges = coalesce(feed_ranges, 0) | eval status = case( feed_ranges > 0, "covered", cpe_ident > 0 AND cpe_ranges > 0, "covered through CPE", type IN ("linux-kernel-module","linux-kernel","github-action","github-action-workflow","binary","hotfix"), "no feed exists for this type", 1=1, "add this ecosystem to the bundle") | eval reach = case(feed_ranges > 0, tostring(feed_ranges, "commas"), cpe_ident > 0 AND cpe_ranges > 0, tostring(cpe_ranges, "commas") . " CPE ranges", 1=1, "0") | eval feed_packages = if(feed_packages < 0, "counted approximately", tostring(feed_packages, "commas")) | sort 50000 - components | rename type AS "Ecosystem", components AS "Components in fleet", feed_packages AS "Packages in feed", reach AS "Version ranges reachable", status AS "Status" | fields "Ecosystem", "Components in fleet", "Packages in feed", "Version ranges reachable", "Status"

viz.option: Every ecosystem in the fleet is covered by the imported feed - the one empty table here that is good news.

panel.title: Did everything the collector found actually arrive?

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_scanstate_lookup | append [| inputlookup riskability_links_hoststate_lookup | table hostname, link_rows] | stats max(said_components) AS said_components, max(said_link) AS said_link, max(arrived_components) AS arrived, sum(link_rows) AS links_arrived, max(sources_failed) AS sources_failed, values(failed_text) AS failed_text, values(swinv_version) AS swinv_version, max(scanned_at) AS scanned_at BY hostname | eval links_arrived = coalesce(links_arrived, 0) | eval shortfall = if(isnull(said_components), null(), said_components - arrived) | eval pct = if(isnull(said_components) OR said_components = 0, null(), round(arrived * 100 / said_components, 1)) | eval verdict = case( isnull(said_components), "collector does not report a manifest", isnull(arrived), "last scan is older than the check window", sources_failed > 0, "a source failed on the host", shortfall > 0, "components went missing on the way in", 1=1, "everything arrived") | eval reported = strftime(scanned_at, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M") | rex field=swinv_version "v?(?<rk_maj>\d+)\.(?<rk_min>\d+)\.(?<rk_pat>\d+)" | eval rk_num = if(isnull(rk_maj), null(), tonumber(rk_maj) * 10000 + tonumber(rk_min) * 100 + tonumber(rk_pat)) | eval swinv_version = case( isnull(swinv_version), "not reported", isnull(rk_num), swinv_version, rk_num < 701, swinv_version . " (below the 0.7.1 floor)", rk_num < 800, swinv_version . " (no configuration surface)", rk_num < 900, swinv_version . " (no Windows library loads or Windows autoruns)", rk_num < 902, swinv_version . " (no Windows build number)", 1=1, swinv_version) | sort 5000 - shortfall | table hostname, verdict, swinv_version, said_components, arrived, pct, said_link, links_arrived, failed_text, reported | rename hostname AS "Host", verdict AS "Verdict", swinv_version AS "Collector", said_components AS "Collector found", arrived AS "Reached the index", pct AS "Arrived %", said_link AS "Links found", links_arrived AS "Links stored", failed_text AS "Sources that failed", reported AS "Scanned at"

viz.option: No hosts have reported inventory yet.

div.b: This is the only panel that can catch data lost on the way in.
div.span: swinv states in every scan how many components it found. Everything downstream reports success whether or not those components arrive, so without comparing the two, a host that collected 3,993 components and delivered 15 looks exactly like a small host with nothing wrong. It then produces no findings, correctly, and the fleet reads as clean. A shortfall here almost always means index-time parsing: check that the swinv sourcetype's line breaking is present on the indexers, not only on the search heads. "A source failed on the host" is the other direction: the collector could not read a package database, which is not the same as the host having no packages, and only the collector can tell you which.

panel.title: Windows patch level, from Microsoft's own build numbers

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_winstate_lookup | eval behind = case(isnull(latest_ubr), "not in the feed", behind_ubr <= 0, "up to date", 1=1, tostring(behind_ubr) . " builds behind") | eval reported = strftime(scanned_at, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M") | sort 5000 - behind_ubr, hostname | table hostname, product, current_build, build_source, latest_build, latest_kb, latest_released, behind, n_installed_kbs, reported | rename hostname AS "Host", product AS "Windows release", current_build AS "Build it is on", build_source AS "Where the build came from", latest_build AS "Build the feed knows", latest_kb AS "That update", latest_released AS "Released", behind AS "Distance", n_installed_kbs AS "Standalone KBs", reported AS "Scanned at"

viz.option: No Windows host reports a cumulative update. Either the fleet is all Linux, or the collector predates swinv 0.9.0, or the bundle was built without the Windows update source. None of those means the Windows hosts are patched.

div.b: This one is arithmetic, not inference.
div.span: Everywhere else on this page Windows is the weak case: the software carries no package identity, so the app matches a display name against a generated CPE and reports every result at low confidence, honestly. A build number is different. The host states the cumulative update it is running, Microsoft states the build each update produces, and the two are compared. Build the feed knows is the newest update in the bundle you imported, so this measures distance from your feed rather than from today: a stale feed makes a stale fleet look current, and the feed age is at the top of every page for that reason. A host missing from this table reported no cumulative update at all, which is not the same as being up to date. Where the build came from matters more than it looks. swinv 0.9.2 reports the running build directly; before that it can only be derived from the cumulative update component, and that component names the servicing branch rather than the build. A Windows 11 25H2 machine on 10.0.26200.9168 carries a component reading 26100.9168, because 25H2 ships as an enablement package over the 24H2 base, so a derived row can name the wrong release while still getting the update right.
